subtopic: the physics of vacuum and gas pressure
sentence: Effusion is the escape of gas molecules through a hole small compared with the mean free path. Graham's law follows directly: the effusion rate is inversely proportional to the square root of the molecular mass, because lighter molecules move faster and strike the aperture more often, a principle once used to enrich uranium isotopes.

Radio-frequency cavities accelerate charged particles through the time-varying electric field of standing or traveling electromagnetic modes. Superconducting niobium cavities operating at 1.3 gigahertz achieve accelerating gradients of 35 megavolts per metre with quality factors above 10^10. The European XFEL and proposed International Linear Collider both rely on tens of thousands of such cavities to reach beam energies in the gigaelectron volt to teraelectron volt range.

subtopic: the physics of vacuum and gas pressure
sentence: Gas flow through a tube changes character with pressure. In the viscous regime at high pressure the gas behaves as a continuous fluid, while in the molecular regime at low pressure, where the mean free path exceeds the tube diameter, molecules collide only with the walls and the conductance becomes independent of pressure.

Quark confinement arises in quantum chromodynamics because the strong force does not weaken with distance: the running coupling alpha_s grows in the infrared. Isolating a single quark requires more energy than producing a new quark-antiquark pair, so quarks are always observed within colour-singlet hadrons rather than as free particles.

Special relativity replaces Galilean addition of velocities with the relativistic formula u' = (u - v)/(1 - u v/c^2), ensuring that the speed of light is the same in all inertial frames. The Lorentz transformations mix space and time: a clock moving with velocity v ticks slower by the factor gamma = 1/sqrt(1 - v^2/c^2), and lengths contract by the same factor in the direction of motion.

The Euler-Bernoulli beam equation E I d^4 y / dx^4 = w(x) relates the transverse deflection of a beam to the distributed load, on the assumption that plane cross sections remain plane and perpendicular to the neutral axis. A cantilever of length L loaded by a point force F at its tip deflects by F L^3 / (3 E I), a result that shows the deflection growing with the cube of the span.

Cosmic microwave background photons retain a near-perfect blackbody spectrum at T = 2.725 K, with anisotropies of order 10^-5 imprinting the seeds of cosmic structure. Acoustic peaks in the angular power spectrum encode the sound horizon at recombination and constrain cosmological parameters to subpercent precision in the Lambda-CDM model.

A nuclear reaction conserves charge, nucleon number, energy, and momentum, and its energy balance is the Q-value, the difference between the rest energies of reactants and products. An exothermic reaction with positive Q proceeds at any energy, while an endothermic one requires a threshold kinetic energy that exceeds the Q-deficit because of the recoil demanded by momentum conservation.

Depth of field is the range of object distances over which the image blur stays below an acceptable circle of confusion. Stopping down the aperture shrinks the cone of rays from any out-of-focus point and so deepens the depth of field, at the cost of admitting less light and eventually encountering the diffraction limit that broadens the in-focus image.

Sticky-sphere phase diagrams obtained from the Baxter model describe colloid-polymer mixtures where depletion attraction between colloidal particles drives gas-liquid phase separation. The attraction range relative to particle size determines whether the gas-liquid binodal lies above or below the liquid-crystal phase boundary; below a critical range ratio of about 0.3 the gas-liquid coexistence becomes metastable with respect to crystallisation, paralleling the behaviour of globular proteins.

An RC circuit charges and discharges exponentially with time constant tau = R C. The voltage across the capacitor approaches its final value as one minus an exponential decay, reaching about sixty-three percent of the change in one time constant. The same time constant governs the cutoff of the simple RC low-pass filter, whose corner frequency is one over two pi R C.

Torsion of a circular shaft produces a shear stress that varies linearly with radius, tau = T r / J, where T is the applied torque and J the polar second moment of area. The angle of twist per unit length is T / (G J), with G the shear modulus. Non-circular cross sections warp out of plane under torsion, a complication that the Prandtl stress function handles through an analogy with a soap film over the section.

subtopic: the physics of diffusion and random walks
sentence: A random walker in one or two dimensions is recurrent, certain to return to its origin, while in three or more dimensions it is transient and may wander away forever. Polya's theorem captures this dimensional threshold, with profound consequences for the efficiency of diffusion-limited search and reaction in different geometries.

Active galactic nuclei powered by accretion onto supermassive black holes produce broad emission lines from clouds orbiting near the central engine. Reverberation mapping measures the lag between continuum variability and the emission line response, giving the size of the broad-line region. Combined with the line width measured from velocity dispersion, the virial mass M = f R v^2/G yields supermassive black hole masses from 10^6 to 10^10 solar masses.

subtopic: the photoelectric and quantum photon effects
sentence: The photoelectric effect releases electrons from a metal only when the illuminating light exceeds a threshold frequency, regardless of intensity. Einstein explained this by quantising light into photons of energy h nu, so the ejected electron's maximum kinetic energy is h nu minus the work function. The intensity sets the number of photoelectrons but not their energy, contradicting the classical wave picture.

Deformed nuclei in the rare-earth region exhibit rotational bands with energy levels E_J = (hbar^2/2I) J(J+1) following collective rotation about an axis perpendicular to the symmetry axis. The moment of inertia I extracted from level spacings is roughly half the rigid-body value, evidence of superfluidity in the paired nucleonic motion. Back-bending at high spin signals pair-breaking and alignment of nucleon angular momenta with the rotation.

Dry friction is summarised by Amontons' laws: the friction force is proportional to the normal load and independent of the apparent contact area. The resolution is that real contact occurs only at microscopic asperities whose total true area grows with load. Coulomb's law adds that kinetic friction is roughly independent of sliding speed, and the static coefficient generally exceeds the kinetic one.

Fourier's law states that the heat flux through a material is proportional to the temperature gradient, with the thermal conductivity as the constant of proportionality. Combining it with energy conservation yields the heat equation, in which the temperature obeys a diffusion equation with diffusivity equal to conductivity divided by the product of density and specific heat capacity.

Doppler ultrasound measures blood flow velocity by exploiting the frequency shift of waves reflected from moving red blood cells. The shift Delta f = 2 f_0 v cos theta / c relates the received frequency change to the source frequency, flow velocity, beam angle, and sound speed. Clinical applications include carotid stenosis screening and fetal heart monitoring, with colour-coded velocity maps superimposed on B-mode anatomical images for real-time visualisation.

The human eye focuses by accommodation, with the ciliary muscles changing the curvature of the crystalline lens to image objects at varying distances onto the retina. Myopia results when the relaxed eye focuses parallel rays in front of the retina, corrected by a diverging lens, while hyperopia focuses them behind the retina and is corrected by a converging lens.

Phonons are quantised lattice vibrations whose dispersion omega(q) is obtained by diagonalising the dynamical matrix of force constants between atoms. Acoustic branches have omega proportional to q at small wavevector, while optical branches arise in crystals with two or more atoms per unit cell. The Debye model approximates the acoustic spectrum by a linear dispersion truncated at a Debye frequency, yielding the celebrated T^3 dependence of low-temperature heat capacity in insulators.

Speckle patterns appear when coherent light scatters from a rough surface whose height variations exceed a wavelength. The randomly phased contributions sum to a grainy intensity distribution whose statistics are exponential, with the contrast equal to unity for fully developed speckle. The characteristic speckle grain size at an observation plane is set by the diffraction-limited resolution lambda z / D of the illuminated aperture.

subtopic: the physics of dielectrics and polarization
sentence: A piezoelectric crystal develops a surface charge when mechanically stressed and conversely deforms when a voltage is applied, because its lattice lacks a centre of symmetry. The effect couples electrical and mechanical energy, and quartz piezoelectric resonators provide the precise timekeeping frequency in watches and electronic clocks.

The BCS theory of superconductivity describes pairing of electrons with opposite spin and momentum mediated by phonon exchange, forming Cooper pairs that condense into a coherent ground state. The energy gap 2 Delta opens at the Fermi surface with magnitude Delta(0) = 1.76 k_B T_c at zero temperature in the weak coupling limit. The flux quantum Phi_0 = h/(2e) and Meissner effect both follow from the macroscopic phase coherence of the paired condensate.

The dilution refrigerator achieves continuous cooling below ten millikelvin by exploiting the finite solubility of helium-3 in superfluid helium-4. Helium-3 atoms crossing the phase boundary from the concentrated to the dilute phase absorb heat, much as evaporation cools a liquid. Circulating the helium-3 in a closed cycle sustains the cooling power over indefinitely long experiments.

Optical parametric oscillators generate tunable coherent radiation through three-wave mixing in a chi^(2) crystal placed in a resonator. Energy and momentum conservation require omega_p = omega_s + omega_i and k_p = k_s + k_i. Continuous tuning across the mid-infrared at high spectral purity is achieved by temperature- or angle-tuning the crystal, enabling spectroscopy of vibrational fingerprint regions inaccessible to conventional lasers.

subtopic: the photoelectric and quantum photon effects
sentence: Photon shot noise arises because photons arrive at a detector as discrete independent events following Poisson statistics, so the fluctuation in the count is the square root of the mean. The resulting signal-to-noise ratio grows only as the square root of the detected intensity, setting a fundamental limit on the precision of any classical optical measurement that squeezed light can partially circumvent.

subtopic: the physics of capillarity and surface tension
sentence: A small insect such as a water strider stands on water because surface tension supports its weight along the perimeter of its dimpled footprints. The support force scales with the length of the contact line, and since weight scales with volume, small creatures float effortlessly while a heavy object of the same density sinks at once.

Bose-Einstein condensation of ideal bosons in three dimensions is a phase transition driven purely by quantum statistics, not interactions. Below the critical temperature T_c the ground-state occupation becomes macroscopic and the condensate fraction grows as 1 - (T/T_c)^{3/2}. The transition is third-order in the heat capacity for the ideal gas, sharpened to second order by weak interactions in the dilute alkali gases realised since 1995.

Chemical shift in NMR arises because the electron cloud around a nucleus partially shields it from the applied field, so the effective field and the resonance frequency depend on the chemical environment. The shift is reported in parts per million relative to a reference compound, making it independent of the spectrometer field strength. Spin-spin coupling further splits each resonance into multiplets that reveal molecular connectivity.

Rayleigh scattering of light by particles much smaller than the wavelength has a cross section proportional to lambda^{-4}, so blue light scatters far more strongly than red. This wavelength dependence explains the blue colour of the daytime sky and the reddening of the Sun at sunset, when the long slant path through the atmosphere removes the short wavelengths from the transmitted beam.

Newton's second law F = m a relates the net force on a body to its inertial mass and acceleration, providing the foundation of classical dynamics. In rotational form, the torque tau = I alpha drives angular acceleration through the moment of inertia, and the analogy generalises to any generalised coordinate within the Lagrangian framework where d/dt (dL/dq_dot) - dL/dq = 0.

Motional narrowing occurs when molecular tumbling averages out the local field variations that would otherwise broaden a magnetic resonance line. When the correlation time of the motion is short compared with the inverse linewidth, the spins sample many environments before dephasing, and the line collapses to a narrow Lorentzian. Liquids therefore give sharp NMR lines while rigid solids give broad ones.

Pascal's principle states that a pressure change applied to an enclosed incompressible fluid is transmitted undiminished to every part of the fluid. A hydraulic press exploits this: a small force on a small piston creates a pressure that acts over a large piston to produce a large force, the force ratio matching the area ratio while conserving the work done.

Renormalisation group theory explains universality at critical points by iteratively integrating out short-wavelength fluctuations and rescaling the system. Fixed points of the RG flow correspond to scale-invariant critical theories, with relevant operators driving the flow away from the fixed point and irrelevant operators dying out. Wilson's epsilon expansion around four spatial dimensions yields predictions for critical exponents accurate to a few percent in three-dimensional systems.

Compressibility effects appear as the airspeed approaches the speed of sound, and the local flow over the wing can reach supersonic speeds while the aircraft is still subsonic. The terminating shock wave thickens the boundary layer and sharply increases drag, the transonic drag rise that swept-wing designs are intended to delay.

Bernoulli's equation along a streamline of inviscid incompressible flow reads p + (1/2) rho v^2 + rho g z = constant, expressing conservation of mechanical energy per unit volume. Application to a Venturi tube relates the throat pressure drop to the local velocity increase, providing the basis for flow measurement. Aerofoil lift arises from circulation around the wing that accelerates flow over the upper surface, lowering pressure there per Bernoulli.

A viscoelastic solid exhibits both elastic and viscous response, modelled by springs and dashpots. The Maxwell element predicts stress relaxation, with stress decaying exponentially under fixed strain at the relaxation time eta/E. The Kelvin-Voigt element predicts creep, with strain approaching its equilibrium value over the retardation time. Real polymers require a spectrum of relaxation times to capture their broad frequency-dependent moduli.

Topological insulators host gapless surface states protected by time-reversal symmetry while the bulk is gapped. The Z2 topological invariant distinguishes ordinary band insulators from topological ones; strong spin-orbit coupling produces band inversion necessary to flip the parity at high-symmetry points. Bi2Se3 has a single Dirac cone at the surface with helical spin texture, making it a model three-dimensional topological insulator.

Jamming is the transition at which a granular packing becomes rigid as the density is increased past a critical point. At the jamming point the number of contacts per grain reaches the isostatic value just sufficient for mechanical stability, and the bulk and shear moduli rise from zero with characteristic power laws of the excess density.

Ground effect increases the lift and reduces the induced drag of a wing flying close to the ground, because the surface obstructs the formation of the trailing vortices and weakens the downwash. The cushion of higher pressure beneath the wing is most noticeable within a wingspan of the surface and assists an aircraft during landing.

subtopic: rotating reference frames and inertial forces
sentence: The Coriolis force deflects moving objects in the rotating frame of the Earth, to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern. It is responsible for the cyclonic rotation of large weather systems, the slow rotation of the plane of a Foucault pendulum, and a small eastward deflection of bodies dropped from a height.

In an alternating-current circuit the instantaneous power oscillates, and the average power delivered is V_rms I_rms cos phi, where phi is the phase angle between voltage and current. The factor cos phi is the power factor; a reactive load with phi near ninety degrees draws large currents while transferring little real power, which is why industrial installations add capacitors to correct lagging power factors.

The dry adiabatic lapse rate of 9.8 kelvin per kilometre follows from hydrostatic balance combined with conservation of potential temperature for an unsaturated air parcel rising in the atmosphere. Saturated air parcels follow a smaller moist adiabatic lapse rate of about 6 kelvin per kilometre because condensation releases latent heat. The difference drives convective instability and underpins atmospheric mixing and cloud formation.

The second law of thermodynamics requires that the entropy of an isolated system never decreases. For reversible processes dS = dQ/T, while irreversible processes give strict inequality. The law forbids perpetual motion machines of the second kind, those that would extract work from a single thermal reservoir at fixed temperature.

The four forces acting on an aircraft in steady level flight balance in pairs: lift equals weight and thrust equals drag. Climbing requires excess thrust to provide the rate of gain of potential energy, and the maximum climb angle is set by the ratio of the available excess thrust to the weight of the aircraft.

subtopic: the physics of collisions and impulse
sentence: In an elastic collision both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved. For a one-dimensional collision between masses m_1 and m_2, the final velocities follow from solving the two conservation equations, and a light object striking a much heavier stationary one rebounds with nearly its original speed while the heavy object barely moves.

subtopic: the physics of explosions and shock waves
sentence: The Taylor-Sedov solution describes the strong blast wave from a sudden point release of energy into a uniform gas. Dimensional analysis alone fixes the radius of the expanding fireball as proportional to the energy and time raised to fixed powers, a relation famously used to estimate the yield of the first nuclear test from photographs.

The Stefan problem describes a moving phase boundary, such as the freezing front advancing into a body of water. The latent heat released at the interface must be conducted away through the already-solidified layer, and the front position advances as the square root of time, with the prefactor set by the transcendental Stefan condition balancing heat fluxes and latent heat at the boundary.

Grover's algorithm searches an unsorted database of N items in time of order sqrt(N), a quadratic speedup over the classical N/2 expected queries. The amplitude amplification iteration alternates an oracle that flips the phase of the marked state with a diffusion operator that reflects amplitudes about their mean. Optimal stopping after roughly (pi/4)sqrt(N) iterations maximises the probability of measuring the target.

subtopic: the physics of dielectrics and polarization
sentence: Dielectrophoresis is the motion of a polarisable but uncharged particle in a non-uniform electric field, driven by the field gradient acting on the induced dipole. The force can point toward or away from the field maxima depending on whether the particle is more or less polarisable than the surrounding medium, a property exploited to sort cells and microparticles.

subtopic: the physics of diffusion and random walks
sentence: Anomalous diffusion occurs when the mean-square displacement grows as a power of time different from one. Subdiffusion, with an exponent below one, arises when a particle is repeatedly trapped, as in a crowded cell interior, while superdiffusion, with an exponent above one, arises when occasional long jumps dominate the transport.

Superconducting transmon qubits operate at frequencies of 4 to 6 gigahertz and are read out dispersively through coupled microwave resonators. Coherence times now exceed 100 microseconds, allowing thousands of gate operations before decoherence dominates. Single-qubit gate fidelities above 99.9 percent and two-qubit gate fidelities approaching 99.5 percent place transmons among the leading platforms for near-term noisy intermediate-scale quantum computing.

Ekman pumping in the ocean drives vertical motion below the wind-stress driven surface layer. The curl of wind stress divided by water density and the local Coriolis parameter gives the vertical velocity at the base of the Ekman layer. In the centre of subtropical gyres anticyclonic winds drive downwelling, and equatorial easterlies generate upwelling on either side of the equator that brings nutrient-rich deeper water to the surface.

subtopic: the physics of explosions and shock waves
sentence: When a shock wave reflects from a rigid wall it produces a reflected shock whose overpressure can far exceed twice the incident value, because the wall brings the already-compressed and inward-moving gas abruptly to rest. This shock reinforcement explains why structures facing an explosion suffer damage out of proportion to the incident blast pressure.

The angle of repose is the steepest slope at which a granular pile remains stable, set by the balance between gravity and inter-grain friction. A grain on the surface stays put while the slope angle is below the arctangent of the effective friction coefficient. Exceeding it triggers an avalanche that flows until the slope relaxes back, a self-organised approach to the critical angle.

Solitons in the Korteweg-de Vries equation arise from balance between nonlinear steepening and dispersive spreading, propagating as travelling waves of permanent form. Two-soliton interactions preserve the individual soliton shapes and velocities, with the only collision signature a phase shift. The inverse scattering transform linearises the equation by mapping initial data to scattering data of an associated Schrodinger problem, evolving the latter trivially in time.

Spin-1/2 systems are described by two-dimensional state vectors |up> and |down> with operators given by the Pauli matrices. Under rotation by angle theta about an axis n, the state transforms by exp(-i theta n . sigma /2), and a full 2 pi rotation returns the state to its negative, the doubly-connected SU(2) representation of the rotation group.

Lightning generates broadband radio emission and an intense optical flash following dielectric breakdown of air at fields near 3 megavolts per metre. Stepped leaders propagate downward in 50-metre segments at 100 kilometres per second, completing a conducting path that the return stroke traverses upward at one-third the speed of light. Peak return-stroke currents reach 30 kiloamperes, releasing about a gigajoule of energy per typical flash.

Synchronisation of coupled oscillators emerges when the coupling exceeds a threshold despite differences in natural frequencies. Kuramoto's mean-field model of phase oscillators predicts an order parameter that grows continuously from zero above a critical coupling, analogous to a second-order phase transition. The result accounts for firefly synchrony, pacemaker cell coordination, and laser array phase locking through a unifying analytical framework.

The no-cloning theorem prohibits any unitary operation that copies an arbitrary unknown quantum state |psi> onto a second register prepared in a reference state. The proof follows from linearity of quantum mechanics: a cloning operator that works on |0> and |1> cannot work on superpositions thereof without producing entanglement rather than a tensor product. The theorem underlies quantum cryptography and forbids signalling faster than light through entanglement.

Stellar nucleosynthesis in main-sequence stars proceeds principally through the proton-proton chain in low-mass stars and the CNO cycle in stars above 1.3 solar masses. Each branch fuses four protons into a helium-4 nucleus, releasing 26.7 megaelectron volts, of which neutrinos carry away 2 percent. The Sun's luminosity of 3.8 x 10^26 watts corresponds to roughly 4 million tonnes per second of mass converted into energy.

Wien's displacement law states that the wavelength of peak emission of a blackbody is inversely proportional to its temperature, lambda_max T = 2.898 millimetre kelvin. A body at room temperature radiates most strongly in the mid-infrared near ten micrometres, while the Sun's photosphere at 5800 kelvin peaks in the visible. Thermal imaging cameras exploit this to map temperature from the infrared a scene emits.

Magnetohydrodynamics treats a plasma as a single conducting fluid with the induction equation dB/dt = curl(v x B) + eta Laplacian B. The magnetic Reynolds number R_m = mu_0 sigma v L distinguishes the high-conductivity limit, where field lines are frozen into the fluid, from the resistive regime allowing reconnection. The solar corona and tokamak interiors typically operate at R_m exceeding 10^8.

The combined CPT symmetry, the simultaneous reversal of charge, parity, and time, is a theorem of any local Lorentz-invariant quantum field theory. It guarantees that a particle and its antiparticle have exactly equal mass and lifetime. The observed violation of the CP combination in kaon and B-meson decays therefore implies a compensating violation of time-reversal symmetry.

Cyclotron resonance accelerates charged particles confined by a uniform magnetic field through alternating electric field gaps tuned to the rotation frequency f_c = q B/(2 pi m). Relativistic mass increase eventually breaks the resonance, requiring frequency modulation in synchrocyclotrons or field strength variation across the orbit in azimuthally varying field cyclotrons. The latter design powers commercial isotope production cyclotrons for medical radioisotopes.

Strong focusing in alternating-gradient synchrotrons uses quadrupole magnets of opposite polarity in succession to focus the beam in both transverse planes. The net effect is stable focusing whose betatron tune nu sets the number of oscillations per turn around the ring. Resonances at integer and half-integer tunes are avoided through careful machine design, and tune diagrams marking dangerous lines guide operation of the LHC at tunes near 64.31 horizontally and 59.32 vertically.

Dimensional analysis constrains physical relationships by requiring that both sides of an equation have the same dimensions. The Buckingham pi theorem formalises this: a relation among n quantities involving k independent dimensions can be rewritten in terms of n minus k dimensionless groups. The technique predicts the form of the drag law and the period of a pendulum up to dimensionless constants without solving any equation.

A helicopter rotor produces lift like a wing, but the advancing blade meets the air faster than the retreating blade in forward flight, creating a roll-inducing asymmetry of lift. Cyclic feathering of the blades, which changes their pitch around each revolution, equalises the lift and lets the pilot tilt the rotor disc to control the aircraft.

subtopic: the physics of diffusion and random walks
sentence: The first-passage time is the random duration before a diffusing particle first reaches a target. For a walker on a line, the distribution of first-passage times has a heavy power-law tail, so although the walker is certain to arrive eventually, the mean waiting time can diverge, dominated by rare excursions that wander far before returning.

Liquid crystals exhibit phases intermediate between isotropic liquid and crystalline solid. The nematic phase has long-range orientational order parametrised by the director n and order parameter S = (1/2) <3 cos^2 theta - 1>, vanishing in the isotropic phase. Frank elasticity describes the energy cost of director gradients through splay, twist, and bend elastic constants, all of order 10 piconewtons in typical thermotropic nematics such as 5CB.

Stochastic cooling reduces the phase-space volume of a stored beam by detecting deviations of small subensembles and applying kicks that correct them. The cooling rate scales with bandwidth W and inversely with the number of particles per sample. Simon van der Meer's invention enabled antiproton accumulation at CERN, leading to the W and Z boson discoveries at the Sp-pbar-S collider in 1983 with antiproton currents three orders of magnitude beyond direct production yield.

Charge conservation follows from the global phase symmetry of the matter fields, while baryon and lepton numbers are conserved as accidental symmetries of the Standard Model at the level of renormalisable interactions. The continuity equation div J + d rho over d t = 0 is the local statement of charge conservation, ensuring that charge can neither be created nor destroyed, only transported.

subtopic: the physics of collisions and impulse
sentence: When a fast projectile embeds in a hanging block, the ballistic pendulum converts the problem into two stages. The collision is inelastic and conserves momentum, fixing the common speed of block and projectile, and the subsequent swing conserves mechanical energy, converting that kinetic energy into a measurable rise in height from which the projectile's original speed is recovered.

The isotropy and homogeneity of empty space are the symmetries underlying angular momentum and linear momentum conservation. In an anisotropic medium such as a crystal, full rotational symmetry is broken down to the discrete point group of the lattice, and only the corresponding crystal momentum is conserved, defined modulo a reciprocal lattice vector rather than as an exact continuum quantity.

The logistic map x_{n+1} = r x_n (1 - x_n) exhibits period-doubling cascades as the parameter r is increased past 3, with successive bifurcations at r values separated by ratios approaching the Feigenbaum constant 4.6692. Beyond r = 3.5699 chaotic behaviour appears interspersed with windows of periodic orbits. The universality of the Feigenbaum constant across dissipative one-dimensional unimodal maps revealed deep structural regularity in nonlinear dynamics.

subtopic: the physics of capillarity and surface tension
sentence: The Rayleigh-Plateau instability causes a thin liquid jet to break up into a string of droplets, because surface tension favours reducing the total area and a row of spheres has less surface than an equal volume of cylinder. Perturbations with wavelength exceeding the jet circumference grow, setting the size and spacing of the resulting drops.

Shock waves in supersonic flow are thin discontinuities across which density, pressure, and temperature rise abruptly while velocity drops. The Rankine-Hugoniot jump conditions enforce conservation of mass, momentum, and energy. For a normal shock in ideal gas with gamma = 1.4, the upstream Mach number M_1 maps to downstream M_2 < 1 through M_2^2 = (1 + (gamma-1)M_1^2/2)/(gamma M_1^2 - (gamma-1)/2).

The body of a violin acts as a resonant filter that radiates the vibrations of the bridge into the air. The lowest air resonance, the Helmholtz mode of the enclosed cavity coupling through the f-holes, reinforces the bass register, while a cluster of wood resonances shapes the response across the rest of the playing range and gives each instrument its individual voice.

The speed of sound in a gas is c = sqrt(gamma R T/M) where gamma is the ratio of specific heats, R the gas constant, T temperature, and M molar mass. For air at 20 degrees Celsius the value is 343 metres per second. The temperature dependence accounts for refraction of sound in the atmosphere, which can lead to focusing and shadow zones at long range from explosive sources.

A waveguide is dispersive even when filled with a non-dispersive dielectric, because the boundary conditions impose a cutoff frequency below which a given mode cannot propagate. The dispersion relation omega^2 = omega_c^2 + c^2 k^2 for the lowest mode mimics that of a massive relativistic particle, with the group and phase velocities satisfying v_g v_p = c^2 inside the guide.

The liquid-drop model treats the nucleus as a charged drop of incompressible nuclear fluid, with surface tension resisting deformation and Coulomb repulsion favouring it. The competition explains the fission barrier: a heavy nucleus must be deformed past a saddle-point shape before the Coulomb energy drives it apart, and the barrier height shrinks as the nuclear charge grows.

The equilibrium temperature of a sunlit body follows from balancing absorbed solar power against radiated thermal power. For a fast-rotating grey sphere this gives T proportional to (S / (4 sigma))^{1/4}, where S is the incident flux. A planet at Earth's distance with no atmosphere settles near 255 kelvin, well below the observed surface temperature, the gap measuring the greenhouse warming.

Spherical aberration arises because rays striking a spherical lens far from the axis focus closer to the lens than paraxial rays, blurring the image of a point. The remedy is an aspheric surface or a stopped-down aperture that excludes the marginal rays. Chromatic aberration, the variation of focal length with wavelength, is corrected by cementing together crown and flint elements into an achromatic doublet.

subtopic: the physics of vacuum and gas pressure
sentence: A Pirani gauge measures pressure by sensing how readily a heated wire loses heat to the surrounding gas. In the regime where the mean free path is comparable to the gauge dimensions, the thermal conductance falls with pressure, so the wire temperature, monitored through its electrical resistance, becomes a calibrated measure of the vacuum.

Heat flow at Earth's surface averages 87 milliwatts per square metre, with continents at 65 and oceans at 100. The total heat loss of 47 terawatts is roughly half radiogenic from decay of potassium-40, uranium, and thorium, and half primordial from accretion and core formation. Mantle convection at viscosity 10^21 pascal seconds carries this heat outward with overturn timescales of order 100 million years.

The triple point is the unique temperature and pressure at which solid, liquid, and vapour phases coexist in equilibrium. For water it lies at 273.16 kelvin and 611 pascals, and its sharp reproducibility once made it a fixed point of the temperature scale. The phase rule of Gibbs shows that a single-component system has zero degrees of freedom when three phases coexist.

Partial wave analysis expands the scattering amplitude in Legendre polynomials, f(theta) = (1/k) sum (2l + 1) exp(i delta_l) sin delta_l P_l(cos theta), each term carrying a phase shift delta_l. At low energy only the s-wave term survives, and the total cross section reduces to 4 pi / k^2 times sin^2 delta_0. The scattering length a, defined by delta_0 approaching minus k a, then encapsulates all the low-energy scattering physics.

Self-focusing of an intense laser beam arises from the optical Kerr effect, where the refractive index increases with intensity as n = n_0 + n_2 I. The peak intensity at the centre of a Gaussian profile creates a positive lens that contracts the beam, eventually overcoming diffraction at the critical power P_cr = 3.77 lambda^2/(8 pi n_0 n_2). In silica fibres this threshold is around 4 megawatts at 1.5 micrometres.

Colloidal suspensions of hard spheres undergo a first-order freezing transition near volume fraction 0.494, with coexistence between fluid and crystal up to 0.545. Above 0.58 a glass forms instead of a crystal because diffusive motion arrests. Confocal microscopy of fluorescent silica or polymethyl methacrylate spheres in index-matched solvents reveals the structural arrest at the single-particle level, providing a colloidal model system for atomic glasses.

subtopic: the photoelectric and quantum photon effects
sentence: Spontaneous emission has a rate fixed by the Einstein A coefficient, which is related to the stimulated-emission B coefficient by a ratio proportional to the cube of the frequency. The strong frequency dependence explains why excited states decay far faster by emitting visible photons than microwave photons, and why ultraviolet transitions are correspondingly short-lived.

A gravitational slingshot redirects a spacecraft by a close flyby of a moving planet. In the planet's frame the encounter is an elastic deflection that conserves the spacecraft's speed, but in the heliocentric frame the rotation of the velocity vector adds a component of the planet's orbital velocity, so the craft gains or loses speed depending on whether it passes behind or in front of the planet.

The Standard Model groups fundamental fermions into three generations of quarks and leptons interacting through gauge bosons of SU(3) x SU(2) x U(1). Electroweak symmetry breaking via the Higgs mechanism gives mass to W and Z bosons and to charged fermions, leaving the photon and gluons massless, while neutrinos receive small masses through mechanisms still under debate.

Rayleigh-Benard convection is driven by buoyancy when a fluid layer of thickness d is heated from below. Convection onsets when the Rayleigh number Ra = g alpha (Delta T) d^3/(nu kappa) exceeds a critical value near 1708 for rigid boundaries. Just above onset, hexagonal or roll patterns appear with horizontal wavelength close to 2 d. Strong convection at Ra above 10^8 develops turbulent plumes that dominate the heat transport.

The cosmic microwave background acoustic peaks at multipole moments ell near 220, 540, and 800 in the angular power spectrum reflect sound waves in the baryon-photon fluid before recombination. The first peak position depends on the angular diameter distance to last scattering, constraining spatial curvature consistent with flatness. Subsequent peaks encode baryon density through their relative heights, with the second-to-first peak ratio sensitive to the baryon-to-photon ratio.

Phonons in solids underlie thermal conductivity and acoustic propagation. In the long-wavelength limit acoustic phonons satisfy the elastic wave equations with speeds determined by elastic moduli. The dominant heat-carrying phonons in silicon at room temperature have wavelengths near 1 nanometre, and thermal conductivity is reduced in nanostructured materials when phonon mean free paths exceed the structural dimensions, exploited in thermoelectric materials engineering.

Diffusion-limited reaction rates in three dimensions follow Smoluchowski's k_D = 4 pi (D_A + D_B) (r_A + r_B), with characteristic value 10^10 per molar per second for small molecules of 0.1 nanometre radius and diffusivity 10^-9 square metres per second in water. Enzymes that operate near this limit, such as carbonic anhydrase and triose phosphate isomerase, are said to have achieved catalytic perfection.

DNA melting upon heating proceeds cooperatively through the base-pair stacking interaction, giving a sigmoid absorbance increase at 260 nanometres centred at the melting temperature T_m. Empirically T_m increases by roughly 0.4 degrees Celsius per percent of GC content because the three hydrogen bonds and stronger stacking of GC pairs raise the dissociation enthalpy. The two-state approximation breaks down for long heterogeneous sequences, where intermediate partly melted bubbles populate.

First-order phase transitions involve discontinuities in extensive thermodynamic quantities and latent heat. Water boiling at 100 degrees Celsius and 1 atmosphere absorbs 2257 joules per gram while pressure and temperature remain constant. Nucleation of the new phase from the metastable old phase proceeds via critical nuclei whose free-energy barrier is the cube of the surface tension over the squared chemical potential difference, dictating exponentially sensitive supercooling kinetics.

Young's double-slit experiment produces fringes whose spacing is Delta y = lambda D / d, with D the slit-to-screen distance and d the slit separation. Spatial coherence across the two slits is required for high-contrast fringes; the van Cittert-Zernike theorem relates the coherence area to the angular size of the source. Illuminating the slits with an extended incoherent source washes the fringes out as the source subtends a larger angle.

subtopic: the physics of vacuum and gas pressure
sentence: The mean free path of a gas molecule, the average distance it travels between collisions, is inversely proportional to the number density and to the collision cross section. At atmospheric pressure it is a fraction of a micrometre, but in a high vacuum it can exceed the dimensions of the chamber, so molecules travel ballistically from wall to wall.

Magnetic resonance imaging encodes spatial position by superimposing linear field gradients on the static field, so that the Larmor frequency varies with location. A frequency-encoding gradient maps position to signal frequency along one axis, while phase-encoding gradients applied before readout label the other axes. The acquired signal fills a spatial-frequency space, and an inverse Fourier transform reconstructs the image.

The partition function Z = sum exp(-beta E_i) is the central object of statistical mechanics. Macroscopic quantities follow by differentiation: U = -d ln Z / d beta gives the internal energy, while the Helmholtz free energy is F = -k T ln Z. Entropy is recovered from S = -dF/dT, closing the link between microstates and macroscopic thermodynamics.

A periodic surface temperature, such as the annual cycle, drives a thermal wave into the ground that decays exponentially with depth and lags in phase. The decay length is the square root of the diffusivity divided by the angular frequency, so the slow annual oscillation penetrates many metres while the fast daily oscillation is confined near the surface, and at a certain depth the soil is warmest in winter.

The wave equation u_tt = c^2 u_xx admits d'Alembert solutions u(x, t) = f(x - ct) + g(x + ct), representing right- and left-moving wave packets that propagate without change of shape. Standing waves on a string of length L fixed at both ends require half-integer wavelengths, giving allowed frequencies f_n = n c /(2L) for n = 1, 2, 3, ...

A magneto-optical trap combines laser cooling with a quadrupole magnetic field that makes the scattering rate position-dependent through the Zeeman shift, so atoms are pushed toward the field zero. The trap routinely collects billions of atoms at temperatures of tens of microkelvin, providing the cold starting sample for evaporative cooling toward Bose-Einstein condensation.

subtopic: the physics of dielectrics and polarization
sentence: The energy stored in a charged capacitor with a dielectric is distributed through the field with a density proportional to the permittivity and the square of the field. Inserting a dielectric into a capacitor held at fixed voltage increases the stored energy and draws additional charge from the source, while a capacitor at fixed charge has its voltage and stored energy reduced.

Spontaneous symmetry breaking occurs when the ground state of a system fails to share the symmetry of its governing equations. A ferromagnet below its Curie temperature picks a particular magnetisation direction even though no direction is preferred by the Hamiltonian. Goldstone's theorem then guarantees a massless excitation for each broken continuous symmetry, the spin waves in this case.

Polymer chains in solution exhibit different scaling regimes depending on solvent quality. In a good solvent the end-to-end distance scales as N^{3/5} via the Flory exponent, in theta solvent as N^{1/2} like a random walk, and in poor solvent as N^{1/3} as the chain collapses. Single-molecule fluorescence experiments confirm the predicted scaling exponents for synthetic polymers and biopolymers over chain lengths spanning two orders of magnitude.

Twisted bilayer graphene at the magic angle of 1.05 degrees exhibits flat moire bands of bandwidth a few millielectron volts, where electron-electron interactions dominate over kinetic energy. Correlated insulating states and superconductivity appear at fractional fillings of the moire unit cell, with critical temperatures of about 1 kelvin. The system provides a tunable platform for strongly correlated electron physics with rich phase diagrams accessed by gating.

Hodgkin-Huxley equations describe nerve impulse propagation through four coupled first-order differential equations for the membrane potential and three voltage-gated channel state variables. The fast inward sodium current and delayed outward potassium current together generate the all-or-none action potential. Numerical integration with parameters fit to squid giant axon recordings reproduces threshold, refractory period, and conduction velocity within a few percent of experimental values.

The Kosterlitz-Thouless transition in two-dimensional XY models is mediated by binding and unbinding of vortex-antivortex pairs. The Mermin-Wagner theorem forbids true long-range order in two dimensions with continuous symmetry at any finite temperature, but quasi-long-range order with power-law correlations persists below T_KT. The superfluid transition in helium films and the melting of two-dimensional crystals both fall in this universality class.

subtopic: the photoelectric and quantum photon effects
sentence: A photomultiplier tube detects single photons by first liberating a photoelectron at a photocathode, then accelerating it onto a chain of dynodes where each impact releases several secondary electrons. The cascade multiplies the original electron by a factor of a million or more, producing a measurable current pulse from a single absorbed photon.

A loudspeaker converts an electrical signal into sound by driving a cone with a voice coil suspended in a magnetic field. Below the enclosure resonance the radiated output falls steeply, and the cone behaves as a stiff piston only over a limited frequency range. At high frequencies the cone breaks into partial modes, and the directivity narrows as the radiating area becomes large compared with the wavelength.

Nuclear fission of uranium-235 by a slow neutron splits the nucleus into two medium-mass fragments, releasing about two hundred megaelectron volts and two or three prompt neutrons. If on average more than one of those neutrons induces a further fission, the chain reaction grows, the condition of criticality that a reactor holds precisely at unity.

subtopic: the physics of vacuum and gas pressure
sentence: Adsorption pumps and getter materials capture gas not by mechanical displacement but by binding molecules to a surface. A getter such as a freshly evaporated film of titanium chemically traps reactive gases, while a cryopump condenses them on a surface cooled to a few kelvin, both achieving very low pressures with no moving parts.

subtopic: the physics of collisions and impulse
sentence: The coefficient of restitution is the ratio of the relative speed of separation to the relative speed of approach along the line of impact. A value of one describes a perfectly elastic collision and zero a perfectly inelastic one. For a ball bouncing on a hard floor, the coefficient is the square root of the ratio of rebound height to drop height.

Seismic body waves separate into compressional P-waves and transverse S-waves with speeds related by V_P/V_S = sqrt((K + 4 mu/3)/mu), where K is the bulk modulus and mu the shear modulus. The S-wave shadow zone between 105 and 140 degrees epicentral distance proved that Earth's outer core is liquid, since liquids do not transmit shear stress. The P-wave shadow zone outside 140 degrees results from refraction at the core-mantle boundary.

A geostationary satellite orbits at the radius where the orbital period equals one sidereal day, about 42164 kilometres from the Earth's centre. Placed above the equator and moving eastward, it hangs over a fixed ground point, which is why communications and weather satellites are stationed there. The required radius follows directly from Kepler's third law with the day as the period.

The capstan equation governs friction of a rope wrapped around a fixed cylinder, giving a tension ratio T_load over T_hold equal to exp(mu theta), where theta is the wrap angle. The exponential dependence means that a few turns of rope around a bollard let a small holding force restrain an enormous load, which is why sailors and rock climbers rely on belaying around a post.

Microscopically, heat conduction in an insulating crystal is carried by phonons, and the thermal conductivity is the product of heat capacity, phonon group velocity, and mean free path divided by three. At high temperature, phonon-phonon umklapp scattering shortens the mean free path inversely with temperature, while at low temperature boundary scattering dominates and the conductivity tracks the heat capacity.

Earth's energy imbalance currently stands at approximately 0.9 watts per square metre, the difference between absorbed solar radiation and outgoing longwave radiation. Ninety percent of this excess is taken up by the oceans, raising heat content at rates measured by the Argo float network. The remaining ten percent melts ice and warms land and atmosphere. The imbalance is the most fundamental diagnostic of ongoing anthropogenic forcing of the climate system.

Functional magnetic resonance imaging detects neural activity indirectly through the blood-oxygen-level-dependent contrast. Oxygenated and deoxygenated haemoglobin differ in magnetic susceptibility, so local changes in blood oxygenation following neuronal activity alter the T_2-star relaxation and hence the signal. The haemodynamic response lags the underlying activity by several seconds, setting the temporal resolution of the technique.

subtopic: the physics of explosions and shock waves
sentence: A blast wave from an explosion is a sharp pressure discontinuity that races outward faster than the speed of sound in the undisturbed air. The Friedlander profile describes the pressure history at a fixed point: an instantaneous rise to a peak overpressure followed by a decay and a negative-pressure suction phase as the wave passes.

Bloch's theorem for a periodic potential V(r + R) = V(r) requires that the eigenfunctions of the Hamiltonian take the form psi_nk(r) = exp(i k . r) u_nk(r), where u_nk shares the periodicity of the lattice. The crystal momentum k labels states within the first Brillouin zone, and the resulting band structure E_n(k) determines whether the solid is a metal, semiconductor, or insulator depending on filling and gap structure.

subtopic: the physics of capillarity and surface tension
sentence: A surfactant molecule has a water-loving head and an oil-loving tail, so it migrates to a liquid surface and lowers the surface tension. Above a critical concentration the surfactant molecules assemble into micelles in the bulk, and this property lets soap detach and suspend oily dirt that pure water would leave behind.

In a periodic structure such as a photonic crystal, multiple scattering opens band gaps where wave propagation is forbidden. Near a band edge the dispersion flattens, the group velocity tends to zero, and light slows dramatically. This slow-light regime enhances light-matter interaction and compresses optical energy, properties exploited in compact delay lines and low-threshold nonlinear devices.

subtopic: the photoelectric and quantum photon effects
sentence: Stimulated emission, the process underlying the laser, occurs when an incident photon induces an excited atom to drop to a lower level and emit a second photon identical in frequency, phase, direction, and polarisation. Sustained amplification requires a population inversion, an excess of atoms in the upper state, which cannot be achieved in thermal equilibrium and must be created by an external pump.

The timbre of a musical instrument is set by the relative amplitudes of the harmonics in its sound. A clarinet, behaving as a tube closed at the reed end, emphasises the odd harmonics and produces a hollow tone, while a string instrument bowed near one end excites a full set of harmonics whose decay rates give the characteristic colour of the note.

subtopic: the physics of dielectrics and polarization
sentence: A ferroelectric material possesses a spontaneous electric polarisation that can be switched between stable orientations by an applied field, producing a hysteresis loop analogous to that of a ferromagnet. Above the Curie temperature the spontaneous polarisation vanishes and the material reverts to an ordinary paraelectric with a large but field-linear response.

Hertzian contact theory describes the elastic deformation when two curved bodies are pressed together. For two spheres the contact patch is circular with radius growing as the cube root of the load, and the peak pressure at the centre is one and a half times the mean pressure. The relation underlies the design of ball bearings, gear teeth, and rail-wheel interfaces where contact stresses are concentrated.

Thevenin's theorem states that any linear two-terminal network of sources and resistances can be replaced by a single voltage source in series with a single resistance. The Thevenin voltage is the open-circuit terminal voltage and the Thevenin resistance is seen looking back into the dead network. Norton's theorem gives the dual current-source representation, and the two are related by Ohm's law.

Anomalous dispersion occurs near an absorption resonance, where the refractive index decreases with frequency and the phase velocity can exceed the speed of light. This violates no physical principle because signal velocity, the speed at which a step or front advances, never exceeds c. The front velocity is always exactly c regardless of how the phase and group velocities behave inside the medium.

Maximum power transfer from a source to a load occurs when the load resistance equals the source's internal resistance, at which point exactly half the power is delivered to the load and half dissipated internally. For alternating-current circuits the condition generalises to the load impedance being the complex conjugate of the source impedance, cancelling the reactive part and matching the resistive part.

subtopic: rotating reference frames and inertial forces
sentence: In a rotating reference frame, Newton's laws acquire fictitious forces that account for the frame's acceleration. A particle experiences a centrifugal force pointing outward, proportional to the square of the angular velocity and the distance from the axis, plus a Coriolis force that depends on the particle's velocity relative to the frame, plus an Euler force if the rotation rate changes.

The third law of thermodynamics states that the entropy of a perfect crystal approaches zero as the temperature approaches absolute zero. A consequence is that absolute zero cannot be reached in a finite number of steps, since each cooling stage removes a diminishing fraction of the remaining entropy. The law also implies that heat capacities must vanish at low temperature.

Escape velocity is the minimum speed at which a body launched from a planet's surface coasts to infinity with zero residual speed, equal to the square root of twice G M over R. It is independent of the launch direction and of the mass of the escaping object, and it exceeds the circular orbital speed at the same radius by a factor of the square root of two.

Lubrication interposes a fluid film between sliding surfaces, replacing solid friction with viscous shear. In the hydrodynamic regime described by Reynolds' equation, a converging wedge of fluid generates a load-bearing pressure that keeps the surfaces fully separated. The Stribeck curve maps how friction varies from boundary lubrication at low speed through mixed lubrication to the low-friction hydrodynamic regime.

A transmission line carrying high-frequency signals is described by distributed inductance and capacitance per unit length, giving a characteristic impedance equal to the square root of their ratio. A signal reflects at any impedance mismatch, with reflection coefficient set by the contrast between the load and the line impedance. Terminating the line in its characteristic impedance absorbs the signal and eliminates reflections.

The Chandrasekhar mass M_Ch = 1.44 solar masses sets the upper limit for a white dwarf supported by electron degeneracy pressure. Above this limit gravity overwhelms degeneracy and the star collapses, either to a neutron star or as a type Ia supernova when an accreting white dwarf in a binary is pushed past M_Ch. The latter provides the cosmological standard candle used to measure dark energy.

The rotating-frame description simplifies magnetic resonance by transforming to a frame spinning at the radiofrequency. In this frame the static field is largely cancelled, and the applied radiofrequency field appears stationary, so the magnetisation simply precesses about it at the Rabi frequency omega_1 = gamma B_1. A pulse of duration t rotates the magnetisation by the flip angle omega_1 t.

Room acoustics are characterised by the reverberation time T_60 defined as the time for sound intensity to decrease by 60 decibels after a source stops. Sabine's formula T_60 = 0.161 V/A relates reverberation time to room volume V and total absorption A in metric units. Concert halls typically aim for 1.8 to 2.2 seconds at mid frequencies to balance clarity against fullness of tone, with acoustic treatments tuned across frequency bands.

subtopic: the physics of vacuum and gas pressure
sentence: The barometric distribution describes how the number density of an isothermal gas column in gravity falls exponentially with height, with a scale height equal to the thermal energy divided by the molecular weight times gravity. The same Boltzmann factor governs the population of any energy level, linking the atmosphere to statistical mechanics.

The temporal coherence of a light source is characterised by the coherence length L_c = c / Delta nu, the distance over which the wave retains a definite phase relation with itself. A laser with linewidth of one kilohertz has a coherence length of hundreds of kilometres, while a white-light source with bandwidth spanning the visible has a coherence length of only about a micrometre, limiting the order of fringes observable in a Michelson interferometer.

subtopic: the physics of explosions and shock waves
sentence: A supersonic aircraft generates a conical shock wave whose half-angle, the Mach angle, satisfies the relation that its sine equals the reciprocal of the Mach number. The pressure jump across this cone is heard on the ground as a sonic boom, an abrupt double crack as the leading and trailing shocks sweep past the observer.

Landau damping is collisionless dissipation of plasma waves through resonance with particles whose velocity matches the wave phase velocity. The damping rate is proportional to the slope of the distribution function at the resonant velocity; for a Maxwellian the rate is negative, damping the wave. The process redistributes energy from coherent waves to particles without entropy production, a phenomenon foreign to fluid mechanics that motivated kinetic plasma theory.

An avalanche on a granular pile begins when the local slope exceeds the angle of repose and stops once the slope relaxes below a slightly smaller angle. This hysteresis between the starting and stopping angles produces intermittent avalanches of widely varying size and has made the sandpile a paradigm for self-organised criticality.

Active matter consists of self-propelled units that consume energy locally to produce motion, with collective behaviour qualitatively different from equilibrium systems. Bacterial swarms and motile colloids develop motility-induced phase separation in which interparticle slowing on contact causes dense clusters to form from initially uniform conditions, contradicting equilibrium expectations that purely repulsive interactions cannot drive phase separation.

The Wiedemann-Franz law states that the ratio of thermal to electrical conductivity in a metal is proportional to temperature, with a universal constant called the Lorenz number. The law holds because the same conduction electrons carry both charge and heat, and it tends to fail at intermediate temperatures where inelastic scattering degrades heat current more effectively than charge current.

Hooke's law in its tensorial form relates the stress sigma_ij to the strain epsilon_kl through the fourth-rank elastic stiffness tensor C_ijkl. For an isotropic solid the tensor reduces to two independent constants, conveniently the Lame parameters lambda and mu, from which Young's modulus, the shear modulus, and Poisson's ratio all follow. The elastic energy density is the quadratic form (1/2) sigma_ij epsilon_ij.
